title: Brant J. Oliver: PFAC, PSSM, and Learning Health System Discovery Set

scope.inclusion_rule: Brant J. Oliver must be an author and the publication must have direct or strong conceptual or implementation relevance to PFAC/patient-family partnership, CMS PSSM domains, or Learning Health Systems.
scope.boundary: No Oliver-authored publication explicitly evaluating the CMS Patient Safety Structural Measure was identified in the targeted search. PSSM items are domain-mapped, not PSSM-specific.
scope.project_data_status: Separate discovery artifact only. Does not alter the canonical 51-source Zotero baseline or append registry.

records.citation: Bartel R, Kimpson C, Lord T, Lyons V, Serge T, Oliver BJ. Patient Experience Journal. 2026;13(1):420-428.
records.title: From Talking the Talk to Walking the Walk: Reflection on Dartmouth Health's Care Experience Week
records.evaluation: Expert patient and family advisors, advisory-board participation, storytelling, co-design, coproduction, and inclusive PFACs. Descriptive; no comparator or attributable outcome estimate.

records.citation: Oliver BJ, Wolf JA. Patient Experience Journal. 2026;13(1):416-419.
records.title: Improving Human Experience in Health Care: Leveraging Humanistic Learning Health Systems to Accelerate Change at Scale
records.evaluation: Places PFAC work inside a care-experience collaborative and humanistic learning health system. Commentary; does not test PFAC effectiveness.

records.citation: Tosteson ANA, Kirkland KB, Holthoff MM, et al. J Ambul Care Manage. 2023;46(2):127-138.
records.title: Harnessing the Collective Expertise of Patients, Care Partners, Clinical Teams, and Researchers Through a Coproduction Learning Health System: A Case Study of the Dartmouth Health Promise Partnership
records.evaluation: Patient and care-partner coproduction embedded with clinicians and researchers. Single-system case; limited causal inference and generalizability.

records.citation: Oliver BJ, Batalden PB, DiMilia PR, et al. BMJ Open. 2020;10:e037578.
records.title: COproduction VALUE creation in healthcare service (CO-VALUE)
records.evaluation: System-level model for judging whether patient-professional coproduction creates value rather than merely exists. Protocol; no outcome results.

records.citation: Oliver BJ, Forcino RC, Batalden PB. Int J Qual Health Care. 2021;33(Suppl 2):ii48-ii54.
records.title: Initial development of a self-assessment approach for coproduction value creation by an international community of practice
records.evaluation: Informs leader assessment of coproduction maturity and value. Early-stage self-assessment development; limited validation.

records.citation: Forcino RC, Jobse BC, Ahmad J, Oliver BJ. Perm J. 2024;28(3):278-283.
records.title: Using Focus Groups to Evaluate a Self-Assessment Approach to Coproduction Value Creation in an International Community of Practice: Phase 2 of the CO-VALUE Study
records.evaluation: Tests feasibility, utility, and acceptability of a practical coproduction self-assessment. Developmental qualitative evidence; no downstream outcome test.

records.citation: Clark KSB, Rudell E, Setiadi D, Agrawal T, Oliver BJ. Perm J. 2024;28(3):284-288.
records.title: Beyond Shared Decision-Making: Integrating Coproduction, Learning Health Systems, Artificial Intelligence, and Workforce Development for Patient-Centered Care
records.evaluation: Connects patient-centered care and coproduction with organizational learning capability. Nonempirical; does not evaluate PFAC structures or outcomes.

records.title: Improving Human Experience in Health Care: Now More Than Ever, We Must Focus on People
records.evaluation: Aligns with leadership, learning, and patient/family engagement. Editorial; does not study or validate CMS PSSM.

records.citation: Clark KSB, Manohar N, Ahmad J, Oliver BJ. Perm J. 2024;28(3):223-233.
records.title: Positive Deviance Theory: Leveraging Compliments Data to Guide Strategic Planning for Patient Experience Improvement in a Large Rural Health Care System
records.evaluation: Uses patient/family-generated data for strategic planning and improvement learning. One rural system and self-selected compliment data limit representativeness.

records.citation: Perry JJ, Hahn M, Kmiec A, Oliver BJ. Patient Experience Journal. 2026;13(1):429-439.
records.title: We'll Be Right With You: Improving Patient Experience With Complaint Management Within a Learning Health System Collaborative
records.evaluation: Complaint feedback, accountability, ownership, and systematic learning redesigned into a measurable process. Single-system QI case; no randomized comparator.

records.citation: Dillehay RT, Verkhovsky S, Bohm A, et al. Patient Experience Journal. 2026;13(1):440-446.
records.title: Documentation and Dashboard Driven Quality and Safety Improvement in Interpreter Services for Limited English Proficient Patients
records.evaluation: Uses standardized EHR documentation and dashboards to make a safety-relevant service visible and improvable. Primarily process/documentation outcomes; direct harm reduction not established.

records.citation: Rizzo E, Adams V, Perry J, et al. Patient Experience Journal. 2026;13(1):447-454.
records.title: A Hybrid Coaching Model in a Multi-Center Networked Care Experience Learning Collaborative
records.evaluation: Addresses leadership and improvement capability across a networked learning collaborative. Capability/process outcomes; no randomized comparison.

records.citation: Vallee J, Stewart J, Verkhovsky S, et al. Patient Experience Journal. 2026;13(1):455-460.
records.title: Enhancing Provider Engagement Through Peer-to-Peer Coaching: The Provider Ambassador Program
records.design: Pre-post quasi-experimental evaluation with matched comparison
records.evaluation: Tests scalable coaching tied to patient-reported experience and provider engagement. Nonrandomized selection and relatively small coached/control groups.

records.citation: Oliver BJ. BMJ Qual Saf. 2026;35(8):503-506.
records.title: Widening of the technical/practical divide: New advances in statistical process control bring new capabilities and new challenges
records.evaluation: Addresses quality measurement and practical use of statistical process control for learning and accountability. Editorial; no empirical PSSM evaluation.

records.citation: Godfrey MM, Oliver BJ. BMJ Qual Saf. 2014;23(Suppl 1):i23-i32.
records.title: Accelerating the rate of improvement in cystic fibrosis care: contributions and insights of the learning and leadership collaborative
records.evaluation: Networked learning, transparent data, coaching, benchmarking, and patient/family involvement. Program evolution rather than randomized causal evaluation.

records.citation: Oliver BJ, Nelson EC, Kerrigan CL. Med Care. 2019;57(Suppl 5 Suppl 1):S31-S37.
records.title: Turning Feed-forward and Feedback Processes on Patient-reported Data into Intelligent Action and Informed Decision-making: Case Studies and Principles
records.evaluation: Operationalizes patient-reported data as feed-forward information for care and feedback for population/system learning. Illustrative cases rather than controlled causal test.

records.citation: Melmed GY, Oliver B, Hou JK, et al. Am J Gastroenterol. 2021;116(12):2410-2418.
records.title: Quality of Care Program Reduces Unplanned Health Care Utilization in Patients With Inflammatory Bowel Disease
records.evaluation: Patient-reported outcomes, monthly SPC, coaching, shared best practices, and feedback across 27 practices. Nonrandomized; individual intervention effects cannot be isolated.

records.citation: N'Dri LA, Waters DD, Walsh K, Mehta F, Oliver BJ. Perm J. 2021;25:21.025.
records.title: System-Level Variation in Multiple Sclerosis Disease-Modifying Therapy Utilization: Findings From the Multiple Sclerosis Continuous Quality Improvement Research Collaborative
records.evaluation: Cross-site measurement of treatment variation as a starting point for collaborative learning. Baseline observational analysis; variation does not establish causes or intervention effects.

records.citation: Oliver BJ, Walsh K, Messier R, et al. Popul Health Manag. 2022;25(1):46-56.
records.title: System-Level Variation in Multiple Sclerosis Care Outcomes: Initial Findings from the Multiple Sclerosis Continuous Quality Improvement Research Collaborative
records.evaluation: Measurement infrastructure identifies cross-center outcome variation and learning targets. Initial observational findings; causes of variation not established.

records.citation: Oliver BJ, Kennedy AM, van Deen WK, et al. Inflamm Bowel Dis. 2022;28(3):327-336.
records.title: Development of Balanced Whole System Value Measures for Inflammatory Bowel Disease Care in the IBD Qorus Collaborative Using a Modified Delphi Process
records.evaluation: Patient-inclusive multistakeholder process defines balanced experience, function, clinical, and cost/utilization measures. Consensus development does not establish predictive validity or improvement effects.

records.citation: Burdick TE, Moran DS, Oliver BJ, et al. J Am Board Fam Med. 2022;35(3):537-547.
records.title: Transitional Care Management Quality Improvement Methods That Reduced Readmissions in a Rural, Primary Care System
records.evaluation: Explicit LHS model, learning collaborative, user-centered redesign, coaching, EHR improvement, and real-time feedback. Nonrandomized exposure and incomplete intervention uptake limit attribution.

records.citation: Davis RA, Sine K, Burguera-Couce E, Ahmad J, Oliver BJ. Perm J. 2024;28(3):245-261.
records.title: Diversity in Combating Complex, Chronic, and Costly Conditions Using a Learning Health System Approach: A Scoping Review
records.evaluation: Synthesizes LHS implementation for complex chronic conditions and highlights heterogeneous structures, processes, and outcomes. Heterogeneity prevents pooled causal estimates.

records.citation: Oliver BJ, Melmed GY, Siegel CA, et al. Perm J. 2024;28(3):234-244.
records.title: A Hybrid Markov-SPC Approach to Assess Cost Differences in Urgent Care Utilization Using Patient-Reported Data in Inflammatory Bowel Disease
records.evaluation: Combines patient-reported data, SPC, and Markov modeling for real-time value assessment in the IBD Qorus LHS. Disease-specific model; estimates depend on assumptions and context.

records.citation: Messier RS, Oliver BJ. Perm J. 2025;29(2):76-83.
records.title: A Humanistic Approach to Improvement: The Multiple Sclerosis Continuous Quality Improvement Collaborative Coaching Approach
records.evaluation: Coach-supported QI inside an MS learning health system using a standardized toolkit, capability assessment, and feedback data. Transferability outside MS collaborative requires caution.

records.citation: Melmed GY, Oliver B, Kennedy AM, et al. Am J Gastroenterol. 2025;120(11):2714-2718.
records.title: Long-Term Sustained Improvement in Unplanned Healthcare Utilization in Patients With Inflammatory Bowel Disease
records.evaluation: Improvements in emergency-department utilization and hospitalization sustained for more than 3 years. Observational sustainability analysis without randomized control.

records.citation: Singh S, Oliver BJ, Hou JK, et al. Inflamm Bowel Dis. 2026;32(4):702-710.
records.title: Real-World Implementation of Treat to Target in Patients With IBD in a Learning Health System: An IBD Qorus Collaborative Study
records.evaluation: Structured implementation across 41 gastroenterology practices inside a named LHS. Pragmatic nonrandomized design; process improvement does not automatically imply site-level clinical outcome improvement.
